mainTopic: Opening a vow with כבוד אב ואם and with a נולד, and the four who are considered like dead
overview: The amud opens with רבא's reason why the חכמים forbid opening a vow with כבוד אב ואם: since that opening would fit every vow, people would stop bringing their vows to a חכם. The גמרא tests this against the משנה, which says the חכמים agree when the vow is directly about the parents. That exception fits אביי's reason easily. It is answered for רבא too: ordinary vows still need a חכם, so this narrow case does no harm. Next, the גמרא asks for רבי אליעזר's source that one may open a vow with a נולד, a new development. רב חסדא points to משה, who was told he could return to מצרים because 'all the men have died.' The רבנן reply that those men, דתן ואבירם, never really died. ריש לקיש explains that 'died' means they became poor. This leads to רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching that a childless person is like dead, and to a ברייתא listing four people considered dead: a poor person, a מצורע, a blind person, and a childless person, each with its פסוק.

steps.title: רבא's reason why the Sages forbid opening with parents' honor
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the חכמים forbid using כבוד אב ואם as an opening because then people would stop bringing vows to a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If so, people will not bring their vows to a חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reason why the חכמים do not let a חכם open a vow with the honor of parents. Right before this, אביי gave a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Almost every vow could be opened by saying 'your parents will be embarrassed by this vow.' If that worked, every vow would look easy to release, and people would think they don't need a חכם at all. To protect the system of התרת נדרים, the חכמים block this opening.

keyTerms.meaning: brought to a sage to ask for release of a vow
if so; if we allowed this
an 'opening', a reason the חכם uses to show the vow was a mistake
the honor of his father and mother

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If so, there will be no vows
brought to a sage to ask about.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: אִם כֵּן אֵין נְדָרִים נִשְׁאָלִין לְחָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second explanation of the חכמים, given alongside אביי's explanation, which came just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים forbid opening with כבוד אב ואם because, since it fits every vow, people would stop coming to a חכם.

steps.title: The משנה: the Sages agree when the vow involves the parents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the חכמים agree that when the vow is about the parents themselves, one may open with their honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: The חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר about a matter between him and his father and mother, that they may open for him with the honor of his father and mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to use as a test for אביי and רבא. This is a setup for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the חכמים, who usually forbid this opening, allow it when the vow directly concerns the parents. The question will be: whose reason, אביי's or רבא's, can explain this exception?

keyTerms.meaning: they open (find an opening to release the vow)

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah:
And the Sages agree with Rabbi Eliezer
about a matter between him and his father and mother,
that they may open for him
with the honor of his father and mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source from the משנה to test the two explanations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the vow is between a person and his parents, even the חכמים allow opening with the parents' honor.

steps.title: The exception fits אביי but seems hard for רבא
steps.stepSummary: The exception fits אביי's reason, but according to רבא, why should opening be allowed here?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for אביי, who said that otherwise vows would not be properly released: here, since he was brazen toward his parent, he really was brazen. But according to רבא, who said that otherwise people would not bring vows to a חכם, why may they open here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה's exception fits אביי's reason, then challenges רבא: his concern should apply here too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי worried about fake openings, where a person pretends his parents' honor matters to him just to get out of a vow. When the vow is directly against the parents, the disrespect is real and obvious, so the opening is not a pretext. But רבא's worry, that people will stop coming to a חכם, seems to apply here as well, so why do the חכמים allow it?

phrases.english: It works well according to Abaye,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אִם כֵּן אֵין נְדָרִים נִיתָּרִין,
phrases.english: who said: if so, vows would not be properly released;
here, since he acted brazenly toward him,
he truly was brazen toward him.
But according to Rava,
who said: if so, vows would not
be brought to a sage,
here, why may they open?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְאַבָּיֵי דְּאָמַר: אִם כֵּן אֵין נְדָרִים נִיתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה from step 2 against רבא's reason from step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's concern, that people will stop coming to a חכם, seems to apply even when the vow involves the parents, yet the חכמים allow opening in that case.

steps.title: Answer for רבא: other vows still need a sage
steps.stepSummary: Since all other vows still need a חכם, allowing this one case will not make people think vows release themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Since all other vows cannot manage without a חכם, here too they may open.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא: his concern only matters if the opening would work for all vows, and here it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חכמים still forbid the parents'-honor opening for ordinary vows, people still know they must go to a חכם. Allowing it only for vows that directly involve the parents is a narrow exception. It does not create the false idea that vows go away without a חכם.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the חכמים fear fake openings, and in the parents' case the disrespect is real. רבא: the חכמים fear people will skip the חכם, and since other vows still need a חכם, the parents' case is safe.

phrases.english: They answer:
Since all other vows
cannot manage without a sage —
here too they may open.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: כֵּיוָן דְּכֹל נִדְרֵי לָא סַגִּיא לְהוֹן דְּלָאו חָכָם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's concern applies to every use of the parents'-honor opening, even in the משנה's exception.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's concern applies only to an opening that would work for all vows. Since ordinary vows still require a חכם, the narrow exception for vows involving the parents is allowed.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's source for opening with a new development?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's second ruling, that one may open with a נולד, and asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר further said: they may open with a new development, etc. What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה, רבי אליעזר's ruling about a נולד, and asks what his source is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נולד is something that happened only after the vow was made. Normally an opening shows the person made a mistake when he vowed, but a new event was not there at the time of the vow. So the גמרא wants a source showing that such an event can still be used.

keyTerms.meaning: a new development, something that happened after the vow

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer further said:
they may open with a new development, etc.
phrases.notes: A 'new development' is something that happened only after the vow was made. The חכמים in the משנה disagree.

phrases.english: What is Rabbi Eliezer's reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פּוֹתְחִין בַּנּוֹלָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי אליעזר's ruling that one may open a vow with a נולד.

steps.title: רב חסדא: משה's vow was released because of a new event
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings the פסוק 'כי מתו כל האנשים': the death of משה's enemies was a new event, and it allowed his vow to be released.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Because the פסוק says 'For all the men have died.' Death is a new development, so from here we learn that they may open with a new development.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by pointing to the story of משה, whose vow was released because of an event that happened after he made it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's vow was tied to the danger in מצרים. The men who wanted to kill him died later, which was a new development. Since the פסוק treats that new event as grounds to release the vow, we learn that a חכם may open a vow with a נולד.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר learns from משה, whose vow was released after his enemies died, that a new development can serve as an opening for a vow.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Because the verse says
"For all the men have died" —
phrases.notes: שמות 4:19. ה׳ tells משה he can go back to מצרים because the men who wanted to kill him have died.

phrases.english: and death is a new development,
from here we learn that they may open with a new development.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: דְּאָמַר קְרָא כִּי מֵתוּ כׇּל הָאֲנָשִׁים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'כי מתו כל האנשים' shows that משה's vow was released because of a later event, the death of his enemies, which proves that one may open with a נולד.

steps.title: Why do the Rabbis disagree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן do not accept רבי אליעזר's proof from משה's vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what is their reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side and asks why the רבנן do not accept the proof from the פסוק about משה. This short question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רב חסדא used 'כי מתו כל האנשים' to show that a new event (נולד) can release a vow. The רבנן hold that you may not open a vow with a נולד, so they must have a way around this proof. The גמרא now asks what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion who argue with רבי אליעזר

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, what is their reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the רבנן deal with רב חסדא's proof for רבי אליעזר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן handle the פסוק 'כי מתו כל האנשים', which seems to prove that a נולד releases a vow

steps.title: Those men did not really die
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the men who wanted to kill משה never actually died, because they were דתן ואבירם, who lived on for years.
steps.simpleTranslation: They hold: did those men actually die? But רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: wherever the תורה says 'fighting' or 'standing,' it means only דתן ואבירם.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push back on the proof. They say the men who wanted to kill משה did not really die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן teaches that the men who were 'fighting' with משה in מצרים, and the men who were 'standing' to complain, were דתן ואבירם. They were still alive much later, in the story of קרח, so they could not have died before משה went back to מצרים. If no one really died, the proof that a death (a new event) released משה's vow falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Did they really die? (asked as a challenge, meaning they did not)
Two troublemakers who opposed משה again and again

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the רבנן are arguing with the פסוק. They agree it says 'they died'; they only say it does not mean real death, as the next step explains.

phrases.english: They hold: those men, did they actually die?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
Wherever it says 'fighting' and 'standing'
they are none other than Dasan and Aviram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by rejecting the proof from step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב חסדא's proof that משה's vow was released by a new event
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The men did not literally die, because they were דתן ואבירם, who were still alive later

steps.title: They lost their wealth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that 'they died' means they became poor and lost their power.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, ריש לקיש said: it means they lost their property.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the men did not really die, ריש לקיש explains what 'they died' does mean: they lost their money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once they were poor, people no longer listened to them, so משה could safely go back. For the רבנן, losing money is not a true new event like death. So this פסוק does not prove that a נולד can open a vow.

keyTerms.meaning: They lost their property, became poor

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, 'כי מתו כל האנשים' means the men became poor, not that they died. So the story of משה does not prove that a new event can open a vow.

phrases.english: Rather, Reish Lakish said:
that they lost their property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the new meaning of the פסוק after step 8 showed it cannot mean real death
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'They died' means they became poor, which is not considered a נולד, so the proof for רבי אליעזר does not work

steps.title: A person without children is like dead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that someone with no children is considered like dead, based on רחל's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: any person who has no children is considered like dead, as it says: 'Give me children, and if not, I am dead.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching, connected to the idea that someone can be 'dead' without actually dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that poor people can be called 'dead.' Now רבי יהושע בן לוי adds another case: someone with no children. He learns it from רחל, who told יעקב that without children she is as if dead.

keyTerms.meaning: Give me children (רחל's words to יעקב)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Any person who has no children
is considered like dead,
as it says: 'Give me children,
and if not, I am dead.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the idea in step 9 that a living person can be called 'dead'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person without children is considered like dead

steps.title: A ברייתא lists four people considered dead
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four kinds of people considered like dead, including a childless person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: four are considered dead: a poor person, a מצורע, a blind person, and someone who has no children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יהושע בן לוי and adds three more cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The childless person from step 10 is on the list, so the ברייתא supports רבי יהושע בן לוי. The poor person on the list matches what ריש לקיש said about the men who wanted to kill משה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, a skin disease from the תורה

phrases.english: And it was taught: four are considered dead:
a poor person, and a metzora,
and a blind person, and one who has no children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 10 with a ברייתא that includes the childless person
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching that a childless person is like dead
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing four people considered dead

steps.title: A פסוק for each of the four
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a פסוק showing that each of the four is called 'dead.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A poor person, as it says: 'For all the men have died.' A מצורע, as it says: 'Let her not be like a dead person.' A blind person, as it says: 'He sat me in dark places like those long dead.' And one with no children, as it says: 'Give me children, and if not, I am dead.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives a source from תנ״ך for each of the four people on its list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for the poor person is the same פסוק about משה, read the way ריש לקיש explained it. The מצורע comes from אהרן's words about מרים, and the blind person comes from איכה. The childless person comes from רחל, the same פסוק רבי יהושע בן לוי used.

keyTerms.meaning: Like those who died long ago

steps.whatToRemember: Four are considered like dead: a poor person, a מצורע, a blind person, and a childless person. The poor person is learned from 'כי מתו כל האנשים,' which fits ריש לקיש's reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא reads 'כי מתו כל האנשים' as being about poor people, which matches ריש לקיש's explanation that the men lost their property rather than actually dying.

phrases.english: A poor person, as it is written:
'For all the men have died.'
phrases.notes: שמות 4:19. This is the פסוק about משה from before; the men had only become poor.

phrases.english: A metzora, as it is written: 'Please let her not be like a dead person.'
And a blind person, as it is written:
'He has set me in dark places, like those long dead.'
And one who has no children, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״הָבָה לִּי בָנִים וְאִם אַיִן מֵתָה אָנֹכִי״.
phrases.english: 'Give me children, and if not, I am dead.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 11 by giving the source for each case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the four is called 'dead' in a פסוק: poor (שמות 4:19), מצורע (במדבר 12:12), blind (איכה 3:6), childless (בראשית 30:1)
